transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Gupta (Redwood AE); Leah Ortiz (Redwood SE); Marcus Lee (Redwood SE); Martin Cho (Helion Eng Lead); Priya Nair (Helion SRE); Elena Rossi (Helion PM); Jamal Reed (Helion Security)

Summary:
Quick dry-run of the cutover/runbook for go-live traffic steering. Focus: canary window, A/B routing for new model variant, telemetry and alert thresholds, rollback conditions, and security/KMS sign-off.

Topics:
- Canary sizing and duration
- Traffic steering / A-B weights and gradual ramp
- Observability: p95/p99 latency, token cost, model quality metrics
- Runbook steps: cutover, verification, rollback
- Security/KMS and VPC connectivity checklist

Action items (recorded above)

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Samir: Okay, thanks everyone for making time. I know this is a busy week so we'll run a tight sync — goal is to walk through the dry run of traffic steering and make sure the runbook covers everything. Leah, you wanna kick us off with the canary plan?

[00:00:22] Leah: Yeah, sure. Hi all. So proposed canary: 2-hour window, start at 02:00 UTC tomorrow, ramp to 10% steady traffic over 15 minutes, hold for one hour then evaluate, then optionally ramp to 25% for 30 minutes if metrics look good. We also have the A/B variant lane ready — that lets you split by quality test set to compare model v1.2 (quantized) vs v1.1 (fp16).

[00:00:47] Martin: Quick question — when you say 10% steady, do you mean global 10% or per-region? Our traffic spikes in EU at 03:00 local.

[00:00:55] Leah: Good call. We recommend per-region steering. The default policy will do origin-based routing so EU can be limited to 5% if you want, and NA to 12%. We'll include region overrides in the policy.

[00:01:10] Priya: And on the SRE side, what's the safe p95 threshold for the canary that would trigger rollback? We don't want noisy alerts.

[00:01:17] Marcus: We suggested p95 < 220ms and error rate < 0.5% for steady state but during the first 15-minute ramp we relax to p95 < 350ms. Those are token-latency observed on our test harness.

[00:01:30] Priya: Ok that sounds reasonable. Also need to confirm circuit-breaker config — after X consecutive 5xx we should stop the canary and route back to baseline.

[00:01:36] Leah: Yes, we'll add a circuit-breaker rule: 10 errors in 5 minutes triggers automatic rollback to baseline. That gets logged in the console and triggers pager.

[00:02:05] Elena: On metrics, can you remind us which model quality signals you'll surface? We want precision/recall on the redlined prompt set and also a small set of safety regressions.

[00:02:15] Samir: We'll push two dashboards: a model quality one with fail-rate on the eval prompt set (we include the prompt ids), and a traffic-level dashboard with p50/p95/p99, tokens per request, and cost per 1k tokens. Also we'll attach a token-delta view comparing v1.2 quantized path vs v1.1.

[00:02:37] Jamal: On security, we need to confirm that the private deployment path uses our KMS and that logs sent to your console are only metadata and not PII. Does that match the SOC 2 notes?

[00:02:47] Samir: Yes — for Private customers we support customer-managed KMS. We'll send the KMS integration checklist. For hosted logs we can redact customer text bodies and keep only hashes and metadata; we'll include retention windows.

[00:03:05] Jamal: Also need SSO / SAML mapping for runbook access. Only a couple of users should be allowed to trigger the rollback step.

[00:03:13] Leah: We'll wire RBAC so rollback and canary-mod changes are limited to the runbook-operator role. We'll show you the role mapping in the docs and include example SAML attributes.

[00:03:32] Speaker 1: (inaudible) go ahead...

[00:03:40] Martin: Walk me through the actual runbook steps end-to-end please, like what the operator clicks and what metrics they look at, and where the automated checks are versus manual.

[00:03:50] Leah: Sure — Step 1: Initiate canary via the Console runbook button or API; this sets routing policy and deploys the model variant if not already hot. Step 2: Automated smoke tests (latency and basic correctness checks) run in the first 5 minutes. Step 3: Ramp to target weight, keep automated monitors on p95/p99, error rate, and QA fail-rate. Step 4: Manual verification by product (we recommend a 5-10 minute spot check): check the sample set, check hallucination/failure cases. Step 5: If all green, escalate to gradual ramp or finalize cutover. If any threshold breached, automatic rollback kicks in.

[00:04:28] Priya: For the smoke tests, can we customize the test set to include EU-specific prompts? Our localization matters.

[00:04:34] Marcus: Yes you can supply region-tagged prompts. The test harness supports tagging and the Console will summarize per-region stats.

[00:04:55] Elena: How do we do A/B evaluation for quality? Is that an online bucket comparison or offline eval?

[00:05:01] Leah: We support both. For live A/B we can split live traffic and compute online metrics; we can also run a shadow evaluation where the new model serves in parallel and we compute deltas without affecting user responses. For the canary we recommend the live A/B lane for a smaller subset plus offline checks.

[00:05:22] Martin: About token cost — we need an estimate of the cost delta when shifting 10% to the quantized path vs the fp16 path. Also how batching affects real latency.

[00:05:31] Samir: We'll send a short cost table: relative tokens processed, expected GPU utilization, and per-1M token delta. Batching can reduce unit cost but increases tail latency; our runtime adjusts batching thresholds during the canary for lower latency windows.

[00:05:49] Priya: Can you clarify the KV cache behavior during a rollout? If we route 10% to a different model variant, do sessions migrate or keep separate KVs?

[00:05:57] Marcus: Good question — sessions pinned to a model variant will keep separate kv cache namespaces. We do cross-variant cache warming but we don't unify KV across incompatible model formats. There might be a brief cold-start for a user moving from baseline to canary.

[00:06:17] Martin: That's fine, just want expectations.

[00:06:30] Leah: One gotcha: when moving from fp16 to quantized we see slightly different tokenization in a tiny percent of prompts; we'll flag those prompts in the quality dashboard.

[00:06:45] Elena: For rollback, what is the human-in-the-loop path? Do we need to click a button, or can the system auto-rollback and then require a post-mortem?

[00:06:53] Leah: Both. Automatic rollback will happen if circuit-breakers trip — that immediately flips routing back and posts an incident to your incident channel. We also keep a ‘manual rollback’ button in the runbook so operators can trigger. After any rollback, the runbook marks a required post-mortem and blocks further cutover until sign-off.

[00:07:20] Jamal: Any legal/compliance flags with automatic rollbacks — like audit logs? We need immutability of the audit trail.

[00:07:27] Samir: All runbook actions, automated or manual, are written to an immutable audit log and signed with the customer KMS key when requested. We'll include the audit export format in the docs.

[00:07:45] Martin: Let's role-play the dry-run: Samir or Leah simulate an alert and walk us through the rollback.

[00:07:52] Leah: Sure. Simulating... (pause) I'm going to trigger a simulated spike: artificially increase error rate for the canary lane.

[00:08:05] [00:08:05] Samir: (narrating) The alert fires in the console: canary error rate 1.8% which is above the 0.5% threshold. The console highlights the canary lane, shows p95 trending up, and suggests rollback. The auto-policy hasn't yet flipped because we set 10 errors in 5 minutes; now we tag the event as 'requires attention'.

[00:08:26] Priya: I'm seeing the alert on our side, too. What does the operator do?

[00:08:30] Leah: Operator reviews the dashboard: look at fail-rate, specific prompt ids, trace a request. If it's systemic, they click 'rollback' and confirm. The system then flips routing, invalidates canary allocation, and logs the action.

[00:08:49] Martin: How long does the rollback take to fully propagate? We need to ensure partial hits don't leak to users.

[00:08:55] Marcus: It depends on cache and the load balancer. Typically under 90 seconds to switch routing at the edge and under 3 minutes globally. We'll add a note in runbook about sticky sessions and expected windows.

[00:09:15] Samir: We'll also include a graceful degrade path: if the canary is sticky for certain users, the runbook instructs to invalidate session keys for the user segment.

[00:09:29] Elena: For the dry-run, can we test both auto-rollback and manual rollback? I'd like to see both flows.

[00:09:34] Samir: Yes, in tomorrow's window we'll first run manual-only with ops clicking through, then later simulate auto-trigger and show the automatic rollback.

[00:09:44] Jamal: Another security item: KMS key policies need to be scoped so Redwood can't decrypt our payloads. We want to rotate keys every 90 days.

[00:09:54] Samir: Customer-managed KMS allows you to rotate keys on your schedule; Redwood only gets wrapped keys for signing actions unless you configure otherwise. We'll provide the key policy template.

[00:10:15] Priya: Is there a way to test the runbook in a staging environment that mirrors production traffic shape?

[00:10:22] Leah: We recommend a staging replay — you can replay a subset of production traffic into the canary lane with headers rewritten. We'll help prepare a 30-minute replay that hits EU and NA ratios.

[00:10:34] Martin: Good. Also, what about burst capacity? If the canary causes a spike in GPU usage, can the Dedicated pool burst or do we have to pre-provision?

[00:10:42] Marcus: For Dedicated customers you can configure burst capacity; for hosted we have configurable warm capacity. For the canary it's safer to provision a small burst so the canary doesn't get throttled. We'll send recommended GPU margins.

[00:11:05] Elena: One small point: timeline for the post-canary rollback analysis — how quickly will you produce the QA diff? We need it for our PM review.

[00:11:13] Leah: We'll generate the QA diff automatically within 45 minutes of canary completion; the dashboard will post the top 50 divergent prompts.

[00:11:27] Martin: Great. For incident communications, can we have a template message that operator can paste to Slack and to our customer success?

[00:11:34] Samir: Yes — we have an incident template. We'll attach it to the runbook and share a copy in the follow-ups.

[00:11:46] Jamal: A small concern: do you redact personally identifiable tokens before sending logs to Redwood? We have PHI in some prompts.

[00:11:54] Samir: For PHI/PII we can configure local redaction or keep logs on your VPC-only path. For hosted you'll want the redaction pipeline; for Private we'll keep texts in your storage. We'll follow the SOC 2 guidance.

[00:12:10] Priya: Anything else for telemetry? We want synthetic traffic metrics, not just user traffic.

[00:12:16] Marcus: We'll add synthetic canaries hitting our light-weight endpoints every minute and surface those metrics as a baseline.

[00:12:28] Speaker 2: (background) okay

[00:12:35] Leah: Alright, let's walk through the exact runbook checklist so we capture it in the doc. I'll read and you call out if we need edits.

[00:12:42] Leah: Pre-canary checklist: 1) Validate model artifact pinned version, 2) Confirm KMS keys and RBAC, 3) Provision burst capacity, 4) Prepare region overrides, 5) Seed test prompts per region, 6) Notify on-call rotations.

[00:12:58] Martin: Add 7) Verify compliance sign-off (Jamal) and 8) Confirm rollback owner.

[00:13:05] Jamal: Confirmed, I'll sign. Also we want proof that logs are redacted before leaving VPC if hosted.

[00:13:12] Samir: Noted. We'll include a proof-of-redact run during the staging replay.

[00:13:22] Leah: Canary execution checklist: 1) Initiate canary, 2) verify smoke tests pass, 3) ramp to 10% over 15 minutes, 4) hold and review metrics, 5) manual QA checks, 6) evaluate for ramp to 25% or rollback.

[00:13:40] Priya: For step 2, what's the smoke test pass criteria?

[00:13:44] Marcus: Smoke tests: <1% QA fails on seed set, p95 < 350ms in ramp, no more than 5 exceptions in 5 minutes.

[00:14:03] Leah: Post-canary: run QA diffs, generate summary, schedule debrief. If green, schedule full cutover window.

[00:14:15] Martin: Anything special about canary traffic steering rules for mobile vs web? Mobile tends to have longer sessions.

[00:14:22] Leah: We recommend session stickiness off during canary if you want even distribution; if you keep stickiness, define a session-sampling policy so new sessions are eligible. We'll add a note.

[00:14:36] Elena: Can we get a dry-run rehearsal timeline in the runbook? Like timestamps for each substep so operators can follow?

[00:14:42] Samir: We'll provide a timeboxed rehearsal script: T+0 start, T+10 ramp complete, T+70 evaluate, T+100 decide. We'll embed it in the runbook.

[00:14:55] Martin: Great. Anything else folks want to call out?

[00:15:00] Jamal: One last security: for audit purposes we need a signed attestation that the canary was executed and whether rollback was manual or auto. Is that possible?

[00:15:07] Samir: Yes — the audit log includes signed attestations per action; we'll attach a signed summary after the canary.

[00:15:20] Elena: If the canary shows a slight quality regression but latency improves, what's the default? Do we prioritize latency or quality?

[00:15:28] Leah: That's a product decision for you but the runbook will surface a weighted decision matrix: safety and correctness get higher priority; small QoL latency improvements alone typically don't justify rollback unless SLA is impacted. We'll include decision thresholds in the scoring sheet.

[00:15:50] Martin: Perfect. Let's confirm the specific next steps and owners.

[00:15:55] Samir: I'll recap: 1) Leah to prepare canary config + updated runbook with session notes and share by EOD tomorrow (Leah). 2) Martin to schedule the canary window and on-call rotations (Martin). 3) Jamal to provide KMS policy and confirm redaction requirement (Jamal). 4) Samir to send cost delta and incident templates. 5) Leah to stage replay test in staging (Leah). 6) All to join dry-run tomorrow at 02:00 UTC.

[00:16:40] Priya: Sounds good. We'll prepare the region-specific prompts and have our QA ready.

[00:16:46] Martin: Anything else?

[00:16:50] Samir: Nothing from us — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the runbook diff.

[00:17:00] (meeting ends)
